messages:
maria: Heads-up — us-west-2 / gpu-pool-7 is spiking ECC correctables since ~03:10 UTC. About 20 cards reporting bursts; three nodes show repeated spikes. Example: node gpu-7-03: ecc.correctable.rate peaked ~48/min. Can we triage before this turns into flapping? :eyes:

sre-bot: Alert: ECC_CORRECTABLE_SPIKE fired for cluster=us-west-2; summary: 'sustained high correctable rate on multiple cards'. alert: https://alerts.redwood.example/INC-3245

ashok: Quick proposal: treat evac decisions as a rate+trend problem, not single-sample. My suggestion: primary trigger = card-level correctable rate > 15/min sustained for 10m OR >40/min instantaneous spike with repeated samples in 5m. Secondary gating: card age and recent replacement history. If card_age_days > 400 then escalate to replace.

lee: +1 to rate+trend. Also: don't evict during 95th-percentile latency windows for customer traffic. Need traffic-aware gating so we don't cause capacity churn during spikes.

jordan: For safety, require two signals before auto-evacuation: (1) telemetry trigger (rate/trend) AND (2) either node-level enrichment (multiple cards on node) OR kernel Xid errors present. That should cut false positives. We can still create a low-risk path to cordon-only in canary pools.

maria: Playbook (draft) — short actionable steps we can automate and also run manually: 
1) Run quick validation to ensure alerts are real: `stackdriver query ecc.correctable.rate by card last 15m`
2) Pin critical workloads or shift traffic via routing rules
3) Cordon node (no new pods)
4) Graceful eviction: `kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30`
5) Run diagnostics (memtest, vendor diag, nvlink check) and `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,count,correctable_errors --format=csv`
6) If corrected errors continue at >100/min across whole node after eviction, mark for hardware replacement and open RMA ticket.

Example commands I used in triage: 
```
# quick per-gpu snapshot
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,memory.total,memory.used,correctable_errors --format=csv
# cordon + drain
kubectl cordon gpu-7-03
kubectl drain gpu-7-03 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30
```

ashok: Config knobs we should add to fleet manager (proposal): `ecc_rate_threshold=15`, `sustained_window=10m`, `instant_spike_threshold=40`, `spike_window=5m`, `replace_age_days=400`, `max_concurrent_evacuations=3`, `traffic_aware_cooldown=90s`. Also a canary flag: `auto_evacuate_enabled_percentage=1` (start at 1%).

devops: We need a backfill run across last 90 days to estimate false positive rate for those thresholds before flipping anything. I'll run a query against longterm.metrics to estimate how many cards would have matched. Also cost note: frequent evacuations increase preemptible reclaim risk and rescheduling cost.

lee: I'll volunteer to run the per-node quick scan script now and post results. small snippet I'll run: 
```
for n in $(kubectl get nodes -l role=gpu -o name); do
  echo "---- $n ----"
  ssh $n "nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,correctable_errors,volatile_single_bit,driver_version --format=csv"
done
```

jordan: For runtime safety: if auto-evac is enabled, require cluster-level concurrency limit and a rollback TTL: if more than `max_concurrent_evacuations` triggered in 10m, pause auto-evac and notify on-call. Also add a simple machine-learning classifier later to reduce noise (features: card_age, temp_history, ecc_rate, driver_version, Xid_count).

maria: Agreed. Immediate short-term action items: 
- ashok: draft PR with config knobs + unit tests for the gating logic (canary default 1%)
- devops: run the 90d backfill and post false-positive estimate by EOD
- lee: run the per-node scan and attach raw CSVs
- jordan: add the 'pause-if-concurrent-evacs' guard in the controller design doc
- i'll add playbook to runbook (https://runbooks.redwood.example/gpu-ecc-triage) and start a small canary enablement in staging. :thumbsup:

sre-bot: Incident INC-3245 created and assigned to eng-infra oncall. Current severity: S3 (investigate & mitigate).

devops: Backfill job queued (job id backfill-2026-03-18-01). I'll post numbers when finished.

lee: scan results (short): 3 nodes with cards >15/min sustained in last 12m: gpu-7-03, gpu-7-11, gpu-2-09. Raw CSV uploaded to the shared drive. I cordoned gpu-7-03 as a precaution and drained non-critical pods.

maria: Thanks — good first pass. We'll iterate thresholds after the backfill. For now we won't flip auto-evac beyond 1% canary until we validate. :construction:
